_about: Registry of the swarm supervisor (scripts/supervisor.py). __CLAUDE_DIR__ and __HOME__ are replaced when it is read. `supervisor.py --init <this file>` copies it to <state>/checks.json. Each check is FUNCTIONAL (does the work), not 'the process is alive'. kind: http | tcp | cmd | fresh | journal | hooks | system. severity: human (a flag shown to the human in a live session + the owner's letter) | infra (the owner's letter only). owner: an agent name or a list; empty = no letter, the check still shows in summary.json and the log.

checks.name: Registry lint: checks look at the result
checks.note: a `fresh` check on a *.log file needs a `fresh_ok` reason (a log is written on failures too)

checks.name: Hooks: files exist and are executable
checks.note: every hook named in settings.json exists; direct calls have +x; every branch of stop-dispatch.sh has its file; imports resolve

checks.name: Briefing watchman is alive
checks.note: chats written to within 20 min -> the watchman must have run within 90 min; quiet chats = green; skipped until the watchman writes its heartbeat file

checks.name: Hooks do not time out
checks.note: more than 3 [TIMEOUT lines in ~/.claude/hook-errors.log in the last hour = an overloaded machine or a slow hook

checks.name: Reminders are not stuck (remind.py)
checks.note: a reminder overdue by over 10 min = the per-minute cron `remind.py --fire` does not deliver

checks.name: Release queue is processed (releaser)
checks.note: a *.ready marker waiting over 15 min = the releaser cron is not running; green when the releaser is not installed

checks.name: Agent cannot answer (API error after a human message)
checks.note: within 20 min a synthetic harness error (API/OAuth/rate limit/overloaded) right after a human message; set `owner` to the agent that should look into it

checks.name: Agent tab is not stopped on a service error
checks.note: needs CCM_WORK_GUARD_AGENTS (the agents list); a tab that stopped on a service error with no alarm adds a line to the agent's human TODO

checks.name: Job under catchup-run: EXAMPLE (copy per job)
checks.note: copy this entry for each job run as `catchup-run <name> ...`: red when the last run failed or the last success is older than 36 working hours (time the machine was off is subtracted)

checks.name: Human presence (informational)
checks.note: present/away is a signal for systems that push messages, not a health problem; red only on rc 2 (unknown). Meant to be called directly, so disabled here

checks.name: Mistakes review (weekly)
checks.note: cron 35 12 * * 0; the log is written on every run

checks.name: Public gate selftest
checks.note: daily 05:25; green and not older than 26 h

checks.name: Quota status
checks.note: file <10 min, source=api, real reading <=60 min; an expired login while nobody works = quiet. NEVER refresh the token.

checks.name: Mechanism code snapshots
checks.cmd: L=__HOME__/.claude/mech-snapshot.log; [ -f $L ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y $L) )) -lt 1800 ] && tail -1 $L | grep -qE 'no changes|commit OK|only secrets'
checks.note: cron */10; the log is also written on failure, so freshness + last line = success
